items.text: The Soviet-led Eastern European military alliance, dissolved with the collapse of communist rule.
The Czechoslovak reform movement crushed by Warsaw Pact intervention, demonstrating the limits of Soviet-bloc independence.
Prepare Western and Eastern Europe in parallel using a two-column timeline, with nuclear politics as a third strand.
Practise one analytical outline answering: “How did Western European integration and Eastern Bloc rigidity develop simultaneously during the Cold War?”
Do not describe all Eastern European governments as having exactly the same relationship with Moscow.
Do not treat the Cold War only as military confrontation; economic integration and domestic political movements were crucial.
Do not say Gorbachev deliberately planned the Soviet Union’s dissolution; his reforms produced outcomes he could not fully control.
The Warsaw Pact was established in 1955; the Treaties of Rome created the EEC in 1957.
Soviet forces suppressed the Hungarian uprising (1956) and intervened in the Prague Spring (1968).
The Berlin Wall was built in 1961.
Communist governments across Eastern Europe collapsed in 1989–91; the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
Study division and integration together throughout this topic: Europe was militarily split while Western institutions grew steadily more integrated.
The Soviet Union’s 1991 collapse should be presented as an outcome Gorbachev’s reforms enabled rather than deliberately engineered.
